bench-wiring.text: For the optional quantization bench only, the violet lead is wired to jack Q7; this hardware detail does not concern course organization or the theory of response and stability.

materials-orientation.text: Working orientation: Lumen is the lecture-note resource and is organised as response, stability and frequency; Atlas is a reference textbook with longer derivations; lab sheets provide laboratory questions. Response and stability should be treated as recurring viewpoints on systems, and the frequency material revisits both viewpoints rather than being a wholly separate module. A noted notation difference is that the lecturer/Lumen convention uses g for impulse response while Atlas may use h. Current lab timing convention is unresolved from the available files: lab-notice.md says discrete-time signals with impulse response g[n], while current-lab-sheet.md says continuous-time signals with impulse response g(t); neither has an issue date or edition identifier, so the conflict cannot be settled from these sources alone. Do not infer learner mathematical ability from discussion of course organisation/materials.
